questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Cairo?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Egypt is Cairo.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Egypt about 1,010,408 square kilometres; Morocco about 446,550 square kilometres; Burkina Faso about 274,200 square kilometres; Jordan about 89,341 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Egypt?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Egypt article.

questions.proof: Cairo is the capital, largest city, and most important cultural center, while Alexandria is the second-largest city and an important hub of industry and tourism.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Egypt?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Egypt on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Egypt article.

questions.proof: It is also bordered by the Red Sea to the east, Sudan to the south, and Libya to the west.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Egypt?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the part of the article about the economy, or at the facts for the country.

questions.proof: The money used in Egypt is the Egyptian pound.
